items.title: Backlog capture: every fenced code block on the site carries empty line-anchor links, each one an invisible keyboard Tab stop
items.body: Backlog capture: every fenced code block on the site carries empty line-anchor links, each one an invisible keyboard Tab stop. Found during the M19-R7 end-to-end check (#53). `zensical.toml` sets `[project.markdown_extensions.pymdownx.highlight] anchor_linenums = true`, but no block shows line numbers, so each code line gets an `` with no content: zero width, no visible focus ring, and still in the tab order. What I saw (built from `main` at aaf83cf with `SYNC_SOURCE_BASE=/home/darren/projects/radiusred`): counting `href="#__codelineno` in the built pages gives 77 on `site/docs/cli/index.html`, 72 on `first-milestone`, 62 on `extensions`, 43 on `spec`, 14 on `platform-interop`, 12 on `working-offline`, 11 on the docs index and 2 on `identities`; each is a Tab stop a keyboard user cannot see. On the homepage the routing example had 18 of them in a row, between the block's copy button and the next link. #53 handles the homepage only, with `.md-typeset .cc-crew .highlight a[id^="__codelineno-"] { visibility: hidden; }`, because the task keeps docs and blog pages unchanged. The site-wide options are `anchor_linenums = false` (loses nothing visible, since no block shows line numbers, but breaks any deep link to `#__codelineno-…`) or the same `visibility: hidden` rule without the homepage scope.
